title: A Autopsy for the Portrait Again
premise: Felix Reyes, the unassuming archivist of St. Aldhelm's Cathedral, has spent years quietly untangling deaths the police mislabeled as accidents, keeping their gift for reading the dead hidden behind locked crypt doors. When a confession letter arrives postmarked a day after the funeral of Canon Merrick—a man whose drowning Felix already suspected was murder—the letter's author claims innocence of a different, older crime: the disappearance of a choirboy thirty years ago, whose body the tide has finally begun to return. As Felix follows alibis woven across three decades, they discover the confession is a shield thrown over someone else, and that their own anonymous investigations have made them a target. The story ends with Felix exposing the true killer at the cathedral's high altar during evensong, choosing truth over the loyalty that protected a beloved institution—and accepting that invisibility, once lost, cannot be recovered.
about_author: Wendell Yarrow is a former parish records clerk from the Cornish coast who spent eleven years cataloguing burial registers before turning to fiction. He writes mysteries in longhand by lamplight and claims he has never once solved a real crime—only read about them obsessively.

chapters.title: The Locked Crypt
chapters.summary: Felix Reyes, POV. Establishes Felix's quiet life as cathedral archivist and their secret habit of solving 'accidental' deaths through documents, ledgers, and small inconsistencies. The emotional beat is controlled solitude—Felix believes invisibility is safety.

chapters.title: Postmarked Yesterday
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. A day after Canon Merrick's funeral, a letter arrives confessing to his murder—but postmarked before the body was found, and written in a hand Felix half-recognizes. The beat is unease: the letter knows too much, including Felix's private inquiries.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. Police Sergeant Imogen Vale, who suspects Felix knows more than any archivist should, confronts them with news: erosion has exposed remains on the tidal flats—remains matching a choirboy missing since 1994. Beat: dread, the past surfacing literally.

chapters.title: The Choirboy's Register
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. In the archives, Felix finds pages razored from the 1994 attendance register and Merrick's name added to a rota in different ink. Someone curated the record. Beat: the thrill of the hunt curdling into fear of what it protects.

chapters.title: Alibis in Amber
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. Felix interviews three surviving clergy from 1994, each with an airtight alibi too polished to be true. Introduce Dean Harrow, charming and defensive. Beat: the sense that everyone rehearsed for this moment decades ago.

chapters.title: A Second Letter
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. Another letter arrives, threatening Felix directly if they keep pulling threads; it quotes phrases only Merrick could have known. Beat: isolation deepens—Felix realizes they were Merrick's confidant without knowing it.

chapters.title: Imogen's Ledger
chapters.summary: Sergeant Vale, POV. Vale privately reviews Felix's history of 'helpful' anonymous tips on three old cases, torn between suspicion and admiration. She decides to watch rather than arrest. Beat: wary respect between two people who both distrust institutions.

chapters.title: The Organist's Hands
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. The elderly organist, Teddy Loxley, lets slip that Merrick visited him the night he died, shaken, saying 'the water remembers.' Beat: grief and guilt—Teddy may be the letter-writer protecting someone he loves.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Tides
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. Reconstructing tide tables and weather logs, Felix proves the choirboy couldn't have drowned where the church claimed—he was moved. Beat: cold clarity; this was concealment, not accident, and the church helped bury it.

chapters.title: The Dean's Dinner
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. At a formal dinner, Dean Harrow offers Felix a promotion and a warning in the same breath. Felix notices Harrow's cufflinks match a description in Merrick's old diary fragment. Beat: seduction of complicity versus the itch of truth.

chapters.title: Merrick's Diary, Half-Burned
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. Hidden in a hymnal Merrick bequeathed Felix, a scorched diary fragment names 'T.L.' and describes watching someone carry a heavy sack toward the flats in 1994. Beat: heartbreak—Merrick saw it and stayed silent for thirty years.

chapters.title: Teddy Breaks
chapters.summary: Teddy Loxley, POV. Teddy admits he wrote the first letter—not confessing to murder but to silence: he saw his brother-in-law, verger Colin Ashe, near the flats that night. Beat: the crushing weight of a lifetime's protective lie.

chapters.title: The Verger's Perfect Day
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. Colin Ashe's alibi for Merrick's death is impeccable—but Felix finds the tide gate key log shows Ashe crossed the flats hours before the body surfaced. Beat: the trap closing, and the terror of being right.

chapters.title: Someone in the Stacks
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. The archive is searched at night; Felix's working notes are stolen, and a candle left burning nearly destroys the collection. Beat: violation—Felix's sanctuary is no longer safe, and neither are they.

chapters.title: Vale Makes Her Choice
chapters.summary: Imogen Vale, POV. Vale finds evidence her own superiors closed the 1994 case under pressure from the diocese. She chooses Felix over the force, sharing the sealed file. Beat: alliance forged between two exiles from official justice.

chapters.title: The Brother-in-Law Problem
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. Digging into Colin Ashe, Felix finds he had no motive in 1994—but his son, now the cathedral's facilities manager, was the choirboy's closest friend. Beat: the sickening possibility that the wrong Ashe carried the secret.

chapters.title: What Merrick Knew
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. Reassembling the burned diary, Felix deciphers Merrick's final entry: he confronted the killer the night he died, and the 'confession' letters were Merrick's own insurance, mailed posthumously by an accomplice. Beat: revelation reframing everything.

chapters.title: Low Water
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. At extreme low tide, Felix walks the flats and finds the second thing the sea gave back: Merrick's satchel, containing the full diary page naming his killer. Someone watches from the dunes. Beat: exposed, hunted, resolute.

chapters.title: Evensong
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. During packed evensong, Felix ascends to the lectern instead of the archive and reads the diary aloud, naming the killer before the congregation and the arriving police. Beat: climax—truth detonated in the one place loyalty built.

chapters.title: The Facilities Manager Confesses
chapters.summary: Mixed POV, Felix and Vale. Daniel Ashe breaks down: he killed the boy accidentally in 1994 as a child, his father helped hide the body, and he killed Merrick to stop the confession reaching Felix. Beat: tragedy—loyalty metastasized into two generations of lies.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Imogen Vale, POV. Vale must decide how much of Felix's interference to report; she files a version that protects them both, uneasy with the bargain. Teddy faces charges for obstruction and accepts them with relief. Beat: bittersweet accounting—justice served imperfectly.

chapters.title: A New Page in the Register
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. Months later, Felix reopens the crypt, enters the choirboy's real name in a restored register, and begins writing down every case they've quietly solved. Beat: resolution—Felix chooses visibility, becoming the record-keeper of truths the law missed.
